extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations; business and organizational leaders seeking PR counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Principles, standards and practical techniques for the work of a public relations counsel: defining PR, diagnosing public opinion problems, planning campaigns, choosing media and tactics, and measuring/leveraging public influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good public relations is good performance — publicly appreciated
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoted definition from Fortune and echoed by industry leaders: "good . . . public relations is good performance — publicly appreciated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR must reflect substantive, positive organizational performance rather than mere attention-getting; publicity that does not result in genuine goodwill is labeled 'sheer press agentry.' Use PR to surface and demonstrate real performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations as a two-way activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic definition that public relations is a "two way activity — proper policy formation and interpretation to the public."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR involves not only informing the public but shaping organizational policy in response to publics; effective counsel interprets the public to the client and the client to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part 1952 definition of public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: As reformulated in 1952: "(1) information given to the public, (2) persuasion directed at the public to modify attitudes and actions, and (3) efforts to integrate attitudes and actions of an institution with its publics and of publics with those of that institution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design programs that combine accurate information, persuasive communication aimed at attitude/behavior change, and integrative efforts to align institution and public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish counseling function from press agentry/publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning that about 95% of information called public relations was 'sheer press agentry' which called attention but did not result in good relations; emphasis on the counseling phases of public relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize counseling, planning and policy advice over stunt-driven publicity; avoid confusing sales promotion/publicity with true PR goals like relationship-building and policy integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation role: advise on actions and choice of media
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel "interprets the client to the public, which he is enabled to do in part because he interprets the public to the client." Advice is given on all occasions the client appears before the public and on the mediums used (advertising, lectures, the stage, the pulpit, the newspaper, the photograph, the wireless, the mail or any other form of thought communication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both the client's actions and the appropriate media; select channels and message forms matched to the occasion and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use demonstrable, positive acts to counter rumors or negative belief
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: to counter a rumor a hotel renewed and publicly announced the maitre d'hotel's long-term contract rather than merely issuing denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When facing rumors or distrust, plan actions that provide tangible evidence of intent (e.g., personnel hires, long-term contracts, investments) rather than relying on denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage credible spokespeople and endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include using nationally known figures (maitre d'hotel, Herbert Hoover, Enrico Caruso) to attract press interest and confer credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and use respected individuals whose involvement or endorsements will lend authority and newsworthiness to the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make material newsworthy and redistribute to new publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of adding content, the consultant made existing magazine content salient by creating a symposium, collating responses and distributing abstracts to newspapers and class journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convert substantive material into formats and frames that journalists and other intermediaries will publish and that will reach target publics (e.g., abstracts, symposia, press-friendly summaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use research and surveys to create authoritative claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: physician surveys to promote bacon for breakfasts; club-women surveys to influence fashion norms; collating responses from leading men to raise a magazine's profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct or commission credible studies/surveys, analyze results, and publicize findings to persuade both publics and gatekeepers; research increases persuasiveness and provides shareable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segment audiences and tailor materials to each public
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lithuania campaign divided material into categories aimed at different publics (ethnologists, language students, sporting fans, American women, jewelers, music lovers, senators, Representatives) and provided correspondingly tailored content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map publics, develop audience-specific arguments and materials, and deploy them where each group is receptive (specialist journals, speeches, clubs, Congressional briefings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ coordinated multi-channel approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective campaigns used all avenues — mass meetings, petitions, pilgrimages to legislators, mailings, lecture platform, newspaper advertising, radio, motion pictures — to 'capitalize the public interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan integrated campaigns that synchronize messaging across multiple media and tactics to maximize reach and reinforce the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage events and ceremonies to dramatize messages and produce images
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: ship launching with motion/still pictures sent abroad; inter-city radio inauguration with mayors exchanging messages; Metropolitan Opera performance to display national unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create visually and narratively compelling events that generate press coverage and memorable images conveying intended implications to broad audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build coalitions and non-partisan committees to demonstrate unified support
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming committees (e.g., non-partisan committee for the League of Nations, Welcome Stranger Committee) and bringing diverse leaders together to show disinterested, united backing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble representative groups across affiliations to lend legitimacy and signal broad-based endorsement; publicize the coalition to influence other actors and the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise bespoke, context-specific tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel recommendations vary widely—e.g., advise one client to give up a Rolls-Royce and buy a Ford, another to change a building facade, one to publish a Bible, another a book of Renaissance tales; pricing, advertising, product presentation and policy communications are tailored individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose the unique problem and audience before prescribing action; there is no one-size-fits-all tactic—adapt recommendations to the client’s situation and publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make institutional claims concrete through tangible initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: opening a post office to demonstrate a community's desirability; founding the First National Radium Bank to show commitment to radium treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete projects and institutional steps that embody claims being made, so the public can perceive real commitment rather than rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PR to educate public and change cultural norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations was used to make previously taboo topics discussable ('Damaged Goods') and to educate on health treatments and material importance (radium for cancer, importance of brass and copper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine factual information with persuasive framing and credible messengers to shift norms and raise public understanding on social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base practice on social science research, planning and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The profession 'harnessed the findings of the social sciences' and emphasized planning and organization (references to psychologists, sociologists and the growth of research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground advice in social science insights and systematic planning; training and empirical research strengthen counsel’s recommendations and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalization and ethics are required goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Prediction that time will provide clarification, development of ethical concepts and the licensing and registration of practitioners as in other professions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for ethical standards, training, and institutionalization to distinguish legitimate counsel from mere press agentry and to guide responsible practice.
